title: Out of Boundary Paths
hints: think of this move by move: how many ways are there to push the ball out using exactly k moves, starting from each possible cell?
define dp[k][i][j] as the number of ways to move the ball out of the grid within exactly k moves, starting from cell (i, j) - conceptually a 2D grid of counts for each value of k
from cell (i, j), one move sends the ball to (i-1,j), (i+1,j), (i,j-1), or (i,j+1); if that neighbor is outside the grid, it contributes 1 way immediately, otherwise it contributes dp[k-1][neighbor]
so dp[k][i][j] = sum over the 4 directions of (1 if that neighbor is out of bounds, else dp[k-1][neighbor row][neighbor col])

base case dp[0][i][j] = 0 for every in-bounds cell (zero moves can't get you out); build up dp layer by layer for k = 1 to maxMove, summing all dp[k] values across k = 1..maxMove that start specifically from (startRow, startColumn) - or equivalently just accumulate the answer as you go, taking every result mod 1000000007
commonMistakes: forgetting to take the result modulo 1000000007 at each addition, letting the count overflow
confusing which grid dimension is rows (m) versus columns (n) when checking boundaries
not accumulating counts across all move counts from 1 to maxMove and instead only using the final layer, missing paths that exit early

content.problemStatement:
A ball starts inside an m x n grid at cell `(startRow, startColumn)`. You may move the ball up, down, left, or right, and you have at most `maxMove` moves to use.

**Count the number of distinct paths, meaning sequences of moves using at most maxMove moves total, that push the ball out of the grid's boundary, and return that count modulo 1000000007.**
notes: maxMove = 0 (the ball can never leave, answer is 0)
the ball starts on an edge or corner cell, needing fewer moves to exit in some directions
a 1xN or Nx1 grid (only two directions are ever useful)

sampleTestCases.explanation: With zero moves available and the ball starting inside the grid, it can never leave, so there are no valid paths.

optimal.space: O(m * n), reducible from O(m * n * maxMove) by only keeping the previous move layer
optimal.pattern: 2D dynamic programming over grid position, layered by moves remaining

bruteForce.approach: recursively try all 4 directions from the current cell for up to maxMove steps, counting a path whenever a move lands outside the grid, without any memoization
